textes.Danemark aux quartiers 1 et 4, Monpezat: Denmark in quarters 1 and 4, Monpezat (a lion and three stars) in quarters 2 and 3: the shield of a queen's husband.
textes.1653–1708 · duc de Cumberland, époux de: 1653–1708 · Duke of Cumberland, husband of Queen Anne
textes.Les armes de Danemark brisées d'un lambe: The arms of Denmark differenced by a label with ermine-spotted points; his marriage adds no English quarter.
textes.1689–1700 · fils de Georges de Danemark: 1689–1700 · son of George of Denmark and Anne
textes.Seul survivant des enfants du couple ; l: The only surviving child of the couple; the shield of the kingdom bears the Dannebrog on an escutcheon, and a label charged with the cross of Saint George.
textes.Le royaume de son épouse occupe les quar: His wife's kingdom occupies quarters I and IV of his shield, the barruly of Saxony II and III, and a silver label shows he isn't the king.
textes.1790–1865 · roi des Belges, élu en 1831: 1790–1865 · King of the Belgians, elected in 1831
textes.Avant que ses armes ne se fixent, une pr: Before his arms settled, an early variant bore the British kingdom in quarters I and IV, and Brunswick, Lüneburg and the rearing horse over all.
textes.1835–1909 · roi des Belges, souverain de: 1835–1909 · King of the Belgians, sovereign of the Congo Free State
textes.Le lion de Belgique porte en cœur l'écus: The lion of Belgium bears at its heart the barruly escutcheon of Saxony: the Prince of Saxe-Coburg becomes king of a new state.
textes.1861–1918 · prince régnant (1887), puis: 1861–1918 · reigning prince (1887), then Tsar of the Bulgarians (1908)
textes.Un lion d'or couronné sur gueules, sans: A crowned gold lion on gules, with nothing Saxon about it; Boris III and Simeon II would bear the same arms.
textes.1815–1867 · prince de Bavière, roi de Gr: 1815–1867 · Prince of Bavaria, King of Greece
textes.La croix alésée d'argent de la Grèce, av: The silver couped cross of Greece, with the fusily of Bavaria over all.
textes.Un parti de Bohême, de Moravie, de Silés: A per pale of Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia, Luxembourg and Upper Lusatia: the shield of a one-winter reign, after which his title of elector passed to the Duke of Bavaria.
textes.L'aigle impériale sur un écartelé du fus: The imperial eagle on a quarterly of the fusily of Bavaria and the Palatine lion, with the elector's orb.
textes.1553–1601 · reine de France, épouse d'He: 1553–1601 · Queen of France, wife of Henry III
textes.Mi-parti de France et de Lorraine : à de: Dimidiated France and Lorraine: on the dexter the three lilies, on the sinister the eight Lorraine quarters.
textes.Un écu qui combine, dit la page, les arm: A shield that combines, the source page says, the arms of both his parents: Lorraine, Hungary, Anjou-Sicily, Jerusalem, Anjou and Bar.
textes.Armes conférées en mai 1429, après la le: Arms granted in May 1429, after the siege of Orléans was lifted: the Maid's sword supports the king's crown, between two lilies of France.
textes.Armes concédées en 1596 à son père John,: Arms granted in 1596 to his father John, a glover of Stratford, and taken up by the playwright: the spear puns on the name (shake-spear). Motto: “Non sans droict”. The crest is a silver falcon holding a gold spear.
textes.Montaigne blasonne lui-même ses armes da: Montaigne blazons his own arms in the Essays (“Je porte d'azur semé de trèfles d'or, à une patte de lion de même, armée de gueules”) and wonders what privilege this figure has to remain in his house.
textes.Un écartelé de deux dessins : aux 1 et 4: A quarterly of two designs: in 1 and 4 a chevron engrailed between three moorcocks, in 2 and 3 a chevron charged with three bezants, between three unicorn heads. The crest, a Moor's bust, isn't shown on the image.
textes.L'agneau pascal est le meuble de l'écu f: The paschal lamb is the charge of the family shield, according to Rietstap and Bouillet as cited by Wikipedia; the link with the name Pascal is obvious, but these sources don't state it.

textes.Armes que Wikipédia dit « empruntées »,: Arms that Wikipedia calls “borrowed”, that is, taken from another family: tierced in fess, with three oak galls, a field of gules and three trefoils.
textes.Les armes de l'« Aigle de Meaux », d'apr: The arms of the “Eagle of Meaux”, according to a register of the clergy of France from 1723.
The playwright's arms, according to d'Hozier.
textes.1585–1642 · cardinal, principal ministre: 1585–1642 · cardinal, chief minister of Louis XIII
textes.Les armes de la famille du Plessis de Ri: The arms of the du Plessis de Richelieu family, which the cardinal bore.
textes.Les armes de Sébastien Le Prestre de Vau: The arms of Sébastien Le Prestre de Vauban.
textes.1732–1799 · premier président des États-: 1732–1799 · first President of the United States
textes.Les armes de la famille Washington, d'An: The arms of the Washington family, of England.
textes.Les armes de Charles-Maurice de Talleyra: The arms of Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord under the Restoration: those of his house.
textes.v. 1405–1440 · maréchal de France, compa: c. 1405–1440 · Marshal of France, companion of Joan of Arc
textes.Ses armes avant 1429 ; il les augmente e: His arms before 1429; he later augmented them with an orle of the fleurs-de-lis of France.
textes.1477–1514 · duchesse de Bretagne, reine: 1477–1514 · Duchess of Brittany, Queen of France
textes.Reine, elle porte les armes de France pa: As queen, she bore the arms of France impaling those of Brittany.
textes.Blasonnement de la page Commons, en angl: Blazon from the Commons page, in English (“Sable, a fess wavy argent between two mullets of the same”), translated into French here.
textes.Les armes de Jean VI d'Aumont, comte de: The arms of Jean VI d'Aumont, Count of Châteauroux, known as the Franc Gaulois, who died at the siege of the Château de Comper. The image surrounds them with his coronet and collars.
textes.l'article donne cet écu pour les armes r: the article gives this shield as the royal arms adopted in 1376, by order of Charles V
textes.l'article dit « three lions passant guar: the article says "three lions passant guardant in pale": what the French tradition calls leopards; the French blazon leaves "in pale" understood
textes.les quatre pals de gueules sur or ; l'ar: the four pallets gules on or; the article discusses their origin, Catalan or Aragonese
textes.l'article blasonne l'aigle impériale (d': the article blazons the imperial eagle (or, an eagle sable, beaked and membered gules) and specifies that, from Albert II (1438), each emperor bore it with his family arms on an escutcheon; the figure chosen shows it double-headed
textes.armes babenbergeoises de gueules à la fa: the Babenberg arms of gules, a fess argent, taken by Rudolf I of Habsburg with the duchies of Austria and Styria
textes.armes des premiers comtes ; après l'unio: arms of the first counts; after the union with Béarn, they are quartered with the cows of Béarn
textes.hermines plaines depuis Jean III (1316): plain ermine since John III (1316); before him, a chequy or and azure differenced by a quarter ermine
textes.la bannière à la croix d'argent sur cham: the banner with a cross argent on a field gules appears under Amadeus III (1143) and becomes definitive under Amadeus V
textes.armes « augmentées » : le tourteau aux a: "augmented" arms: the roundel with the arms of France was granted by Louis XI in 1465
textes.l'article décrit le drapeau de Gênes, la: the article describes the flag of Genoa, the red cross of Saint George on a white ground, the same design as the shield
textes.blasonnement donné par la page du fichie: blazon given by the file page; Wikipedia (en), "Teutonic Order" mentions the white surcoat with a black cross
textes.armes de l'Ordre de Malte, héritier des: arms of the Order of Malta, heir of the Hospitallers

textes.forme en usage à partir de Pierre IV le: form in use from Peter IV the Ceremonious; the crown was granted in 1377

textes.section « Wappen », traduite de l'allema: "Wappen" section, translated from German; the article dates these arms to 1804 (before: two or three gold crowns on a blue field), after Franz Gall, "Österreichische Wappenkunde"

textes.en 1431, Charles VII leur concède un éca: in 1431, Charles VII granted them a quarterly with the lilies of France; the file shows the earlier arms
textes.la disposition 3, 2 et 1 d'après la page: the 3, 2 and 1 arrangement comes from the file's Commons page

textes.l'article écrit « au lion contourné cour: the article writes "au lion contourné couronné d'or, armé, lampassé et couronné de gueules": it gives the crown two tinctures; we keep the second, that of the image

textes.armes de la ville, que l'article dit êtr: arms of the city, which the article says are those "of the domain and county of Mechelen": the pales of the Berthouts, and the eagle granted by Frederick III in 1490; the drawing follows Guicciardini (1581)
textes.« het zilveren kruis op rode achtergrond: "het zilveren kruis op rode achtergrond", on the seal of Bishop John of Sierck from 1291

textes.La page lue donne ces armes à la ligne d: The page read gives these arms to the family line; it gives the emperors of the house a single-headed eagle sable on or, with these lions overall. The file is named "Arms of Swabia".
textes.Le fichier se nomme « Nord-Pas-de-Calais: The file is named "Nord-Pas-de-Calais"; the page read uses it for the lion of Meissen.
textes.Othon Ier reçoit en 1180 de Frédéric Bar: Otto I received from Frederick Barbarossa in 1180 the Duchy of Bavaria, confiscated from Henry the Lion; the page gives this fusily for the Dukes of Bavaria from 1180 to 1623.
textes.Il s'agissait à l'origine de trois aigle: Originally these were three eaglets whose legs and beak atrophied to become the present alerion, at the end of the 15th century (page read).
textes.armes dites « à enquerre » : un métal (l: so-called "enquire" arms: a metal (or) placed on a metal (argent), against the rule of tincture
textes.les rois de Chypre portaient « burelé d': the Kings of Cyprus bore "burelé d'argent et d'azur au lion de gueules, armé, lampassé et couronné d'or, brochant"; the file's Commons page specifies ten pieces

textes.l'image montre aussi l'aigle qui porte l: the image also shows the eagle bearing the shield, its cross, branch and sceptre, which the blazon of the shield doesn't mention

textes.l'article décrit, pour la branche danois: the article describes, for the Danish branch, a shield "delad i fem bjälkar i guld och rött" (five bars or and gules) charged with bezants or, whose number varies from one sentence to the next; here, the eight bezants 3, 3 and 2 are read from the Commons image

textes.Les cinq tourteaux sont posés 2, 2 et 1: The five torteaux are set 2, 2 and 1 as on the image; the azure roundel bears three fleurs-de-lis, two and one, reduced and spaced apart (settings cs and ce).
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : la de: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: the Nasrid motto in Arabic letters isn't drawn.
textes.Le dessin ne reprend que l'écu : l'Ateli: The drawing shows only the shield: the Atelier draws neither the lozenge shape nor the royal crown
textes.L'aigle impériale est la figure de Sodac: The imperial eagle is Sodacan's figure, with the thunderbolt beneath the talons: the text read by the Atelier doesn't say "grasping a thunderbolt", it is part of the figure.
textes.Le dessin ne reprend pas le double tresc: The drawing leaves out the double tressure flory counter-flory around the lion of Scotland
textes.La croix est affinée (épaisseur 55 %) po: The cross is thinned (55% thickness) to follow the image; the arms of the shield alone, without supporters or crown.
textes.Le dessin compte seize compons (la sourc: The drawing has sixteen compons (the source doesn't give the number) and shows a towered castle
textes.Le saint Ferdinand garde ses couleurs pr: Saint Ferdinand keeps his own colours (flesh, azure, or, a throne or): the tincture stated after his name changes nothing. The lions and castles of the bordure are the Atelier's.
textes.Le dessin ne reprend pas ce que le lion: The drawing leaves out what the lion holds (a sword and a sheaf of seven arrows)
textes.Le dessin ne reprend que l'écu : l'Ateli: The drawing shows only the shield: the Atelier doesn't read the crest and helm (helm argent crowned or, plume of peacock feathers, mantling azure)
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : le pa: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: the landscape (confluence of the Euphrates and Tigris, palm trees, Hakkari mountains) can't be drawn; the sword and spear in saltire are suggested by two swords.
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : l'épé: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: the sword and the lion couchant; the sceptre in saltire, the donkey couchant and the eight-pointed star sable in chief remain to be added.
textes.Le casque de Skanderbeg est posé en chef: The helmet of Skanderbeg is set in chief, reduced and raised above the eagle (in the arms it surmounts the shield); the Atelier's "Ajuster" settings move it as you wish.
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : deux: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: only two spears; the commander's baton, the two sabres, the spearheads and the tassels remain to be added.
textes.Le trait du coupé est droit dans l'Ateli: The line of the per fess is straight in the Atelier; on the image, the lion emerges from the first wave
textes.Les châteaux d'Artois sont ceux de Casti: The castles of Artois are those of Castile, with three towers: the Atelier calls them "châteaux donjonnés"
textes.La traverse de l'image va de l'angle dex: The image's traverse runs from the dexter corner of the chief towards the base: the Atelier draws it as a bendlet, a narrow bend
textes.L'Atelier dessine ici son aigle éployée: The Atelier draws its one-headed displayed eagle here, entirely sable (its crown is given the same tincture); the escutcheon is larger than on the image.
textes.L'Atelier dessine l'ours passant, qui mo: The Atelier draws the bear passant, climbing along the broad bend, as on the image
textes.Le dessin ne reprend ni les yeux d'argen: The drawing leaves out the argent eyes (allumé), and the ring through the muzzle and the gules tongue (bouclé et langué)
textes.La source dit « à la croisette d'argent,: The source says "à la croisette d'argent, au franc-quartier senestre": the Atelier sets it in a sinister quarter of the tincture of the field
textes.Le dessin ne montre pas le double pannet: The drawing doesn't show the key's double ward
textes.Saint Fridolin est dessiné d'après les a: Saint Fridolin is drawn after the arms of the canton (nimbus, staff and book or); the "proper" of the blazon isn't rendered by the tincture.
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : bélie: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: ram passant instead of salient; crown, hooves, horns and pizzle of the field to be set.
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : l'our: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: the bear has no gules claws; the V and R of the second aren't drawn.
textes.Le blasonnement ne dit pas l'attitude de: The blazon doesn't give the bear's attitude; on the image it stands erect: the Atelier calls it "ours rampant"
textes.La rivière se dessine en trois fasces on: The river is drawn as three bars wavy; the three stars "grouped at the fess point" are set 2 and 1
textes.Le blasonnement dit « à deux lions … pos: The blazon says "two lions … set along the line of the division": the Atelier sets one lion in each part
textes.Le dessin ne reprend pas la devise inscr: The drawing leaves out the motto written on the argent
textes.La croix d'argent du gueules est posée a: The argent cross on the gules is set in the sinister corner of the chief (it is "over all" in the Atelier); on the image, it is higher and thinner.
textes.L'aigle fédérale est la figure du Bundes: The federal eagle is Schwab's Bundesadler figure (public domain): beak and talons gules; the card's drawing is in an older style, with less elongated wings.
textes.Les deux vaches du Béarn sont dessinées: The two cows of Béarn are drawn one above the other ("passant in pale"); the crozier is set bendwise sinister under the mitre.
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : les d: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: the two eagles' heads respectant are two eagles; the lion and the leopard don't carry their cross; the orange escutcheon with the ark is a mount or (the orange and the ark are missing).
textes.Les étoiles « accolées en bande » longen: The stars "set bendwise" follow the line of the per bend: the Atelier calls them "posées en bande"; on the image, the line doesn't quite start from the corner of the chief
textes.La source ne dit pas l'émail de la colom: The source doesn't give the dove's tincture: the Atelier draws it argent; the branch is olive, green
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : seul: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: only the chequy of twenty-five pieces is drawn; the crown of five shields remains to be added.
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : les n: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: the nine hearts are ranged 3, 3 and 3 beside the three lions instead of slipping between them; the ram and the bear are the Atelier's figures (ram passant, bear rampant), without the image's details.
textes.Le dessin ne reprend ni l'épée haute ni: The drawing leaves out the raised sword and the scimitar held by the lion
textes.Le saint terrasse un dragon sur le dessi: The saint strikes down a dragon in the drawing (the blazon says a serpent) and his nimbus isn't gold: the Atelier doesn't colour the figure in several tinctures.
textes.Ébauche à ajuster dans l'Atelier : la cr: Draft to adjust in the Atelier: the patriarchal cross is drawn as a cross of Lorraine; the crown and the triple mount vert are missing.
